$comment: Receiver side of the owner decision of 2026-11-06 on #176 item 18. The envelope, `__VALID_JWT__` minting and `self_trust_anchors` are mh-012's, so steps 1 to 7 of RFC-AITP-0004 §5.1 pass and the step 8 trust-anchor check would pass. Only `self_accepted_identity_types` differs: `["did", "example-type"]`, a Reserved name and a name in no registry row. This is the receiver-side counterpart of man-014, whose fetcher-side screen no operation can pin.
description: The receiver's own `accepted_identity_types` lists only types it does not implement (`did`, `example-type`), and the initiator presents a valid `oidc` identity from an issuer the receiver trusts. The list accepts no type. Step 8 MUST reject with INCOMPATIBLE_IDENTITY_TYPE.

expected.rationale: Neither entry is a type the receiver implements, so both are ignored and the list accepts no type, as an explicit `[]` does (RFC-AITP-0003 §3.2, §5 step 6; RFC-AITP-0004 §5.1 step 8). A verifier that falls back to the default `["oidc"]` when it recognises no entry accepts the peer and fails this fixture; the default applies only when the field is absent.
